message.content:
A cell that contains more than one nucleus is called a **multinucleated cell**.  
In biology, such cells are often referred to as a **syncytium** (plural *syncytia*). Syncytia can form naturally—e.g., skeletal muscle fibers (myocytes) and osteoclasts—or they can arise during certain infections (e.g., syncytial giant cells seen in tuberculosis or sarcoidosis).
